summary: Titled mutual, but the definition and every operative obligation (confidentiality, return, equitable relief, costs) bind only Halyard, with other deviations on carve-outs, personal data, derivative works and backups.

findings.quote: disclosed by or on behalf of Vedanta to Halyard, or otherwise obtained or accessed by Halyard in connection with the Business Purpose
findings.why: The agreement is titled mutual but Confidential Information covers only Vedanta's information and clauses 2 to 9 bind only Halyard as recipient.
findings.draft_redline: "Confidential Information means any information disclosed by or on behalf of the Disclosing Party to the Receiving Party in connection with the Purpose that is marked confidential or would reasonably be considered confidential, including notes and analyses derived from it." Restate clause 2 so that it binds the Receiving Party, and either Party may be the Receiving Party.
findings.note_to_counterparty: As this is a mutual NDA, both parties will be disclosing, so we have made the definition and obligations apply equally to each of us.

findings.quote: Halyard acknowledges and agrees that the Confidential Information disclosed to it contains valuable business assets and trade secrets of Vedanta. Accordingly, Halyard undertakes to:
findings.why: The operative confidentiality undertakings are given by Halyard alone, so Halyard's own disclosures receive no protection.
findings.draft_redline: "Each Party, as Receiving Party, undertakes to the Disclosing Party to:" followed by the clause 2.1 undertakings.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the confidentiality undertakings to apply to both parties as receiving party, in line with the mutual title.

findings.quote: or otherwise obtained or accessed by Halyard in connection with the Business Purpose, whether disclosed prior to, on, or after the Effective Date
findings.why: The definition extends to information merely accessed by Halyard and to information received before the Effective Date, not only information disclosed for the Purpose, and has no marking or reasonable-confidentiality test.
findings.draft_redline: Limit the definition to information disclosed for the Purpose that is marked confidential or would reasonably be considered confidential.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We suggest tying the definition to information actually disclosed for the Business Purpose that is marked or reasonably confidential.

findings.quote: for any purpose other than the direct evaluation and execution of the Business Purpose
findings.why: Use is limited to the Business Purpose, which is the evaluation of a prospective collaboration, though the word 'execution' is slightly wider than evaluation.

findings.quote: was independently developed by Halyard's personnel without any access to, reliance upon, or reference to the Confidential Information of Vedanta
findings.why: The independent development carve-out is narrowed by a no-access, no-reference test and by the contemporaneous written evidence standard in 3.1.
findings.draft_redline: "was independently developed by or for the Receiving Party without use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information."
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the independent development exclusion to be the standard formulation.

findings.quote: that Halyard can clearly demonstrate by contemporaneous written evidence:
findings.why: The carve-outs require clear demonstration by contemporaneous written evidence, which is stricter than the acceptable 'written records' or 'reasonable evidence' standard, and there is no carve-out for information lawfully received from a third party.
findings.draft_redline: "that the Receiving Party can show by written records: ... (c) was lawfully received from a third party without restriction on disclosure; ..." Delete 3.1.4 as an exclusion and add the third-party-receipt exclusion.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like to add the usual exclusion for information received lawfully from a third party and to apply a written-records evidence standard.

findings.quote: directors, officers, employees, legal advisers, accountants, and consultants of a Party and of its Affiliates
findings.why: Representatives cover Affiliates, advisers and accountants but not insurers or expressly auditors, and 2.1.5 separately requires Vedanta's written consent for any third-party disclosure.
findings.draft_redline: Add 'professional advisers, auditors, insurers' to the definition of Representatives and make clause 2.1.5 subject to permitted disclosure to Representatives.
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please add auditors and insurers to the permitted recipients and make clear that 2.1.5 does not override disclosure to Representatives.

findings.quote: to the extent permitted by law, provide Vedanta with prompt written notice within three (3) Business Days of receiving such request or demand
findings.why: Disclosure is permitted where legally required, notice is qualified by 'to the extent permitted by law', and cooperation and reasonable endeavours are at Vedanta's expense.
findings.fallback_cited: Notice 'where lawful' and cooperation at the Disclosing Party's cost.

findings.quote: Halyard may retain one (1) copy of the Confidential Information solely in its legal archives to the extent strictly necessary to comply with applicable statutory, regulatory, or professional record-retention requirements
findings.why: The only retention exception is a single legal-archive copy, with no exception for automated backups.
findings.draft_redline: Add: "The Receiving Party may retain copies held in automated electronic backups, and copies it is required to keep by law or regulation, provided they remain subject to this Agreement and are not accessed except as legally required."
findings.note_to_counterparty: Please add a short exception for automated backup copies, which cannot practically be deleted; they would remain confidential.

findings.quote: All Confidential Information, including all copies, extracts, adaptations, and derivative works thereof, shall remain the sole and exclusive property of Vedanta or its licensors.
findings.why: Derivative works and adaptations, which could include Halyard's own work, are vested in Vedanta, and ownership is stated for Vedanta only.
findings.draft_redline: "Each Party retains all right, title and interest in its own Confidential Information and intellectual property, and no licence is granted other than the right to use the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information for the Purpose."
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the IP wording to be mutual and not to vest in either party material developed independently by the other.

findings.quote: Vedanta shall not be liable to Halyard or to any other person for any direct, indirect, consequential, punitive, or incidental damages or losses arising out of or resulting from the use of, or reliance upon, any Confidential Information
findings.why: The liability exclusion has no fraud carve-out and the disclaimer protects only Vedanta, not Halyard.
findings.draft_redline: "Neither Party shall be liable to the other for use of or reliance on the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information, save in the case of fraud."
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the disclaimer to be mutual and to preserve liability for fraud.

findings.quote: all employee profiles, contractor records, personal identification data, performance appraisals, compensation details, and candidate CVs supplied in connection with prospective resource allocation or project staffing
findings.why: The definition expressly contemplates sharing employee and candidate personal data, but the agreement has no data protection terms or DPA commitment.
findings.draft_redline: "The Parties shall not share personal data beyond business contact details unless they first enter into a separate data processing or data sharing agreement, and each Party shall comply with UK GDPR and EU GDPR."
findings.note_to_counterparty: If personal data will be exchanged, we would need a data processing or sharing agreement in place first; otherwise please limit sharing to business contact details.

findings.quote: an initial term of two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party upon giving thirty (30) calendar days' written notice
findings.why: A two-year term with 30 days' notice matches the preferred term.

findings.quote: for a period of three (3) years from the effective date of termination or expiration, except that in respect of any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law, such obligations shall survive indefinitely for as long as such information remains a trade secret
findings.why: Three-year survival with trade secrets protected while they remain trade secrets matches the preferred position.

findings.quote: Vedanta shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief, specific performance, and other equitable remedies before any court of competent jurisdiction, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond or other security
findings.why: The right to equitable relief belongs to Vedanta only, so Halyard has no equivalent right.
findings.draft_redline: "Each Party may seek injunctive relief and other equitable remedies for any actual or threatened breach by the other, in addition to any other remedies."
findings.note_to_counterparty: We would like the equitable relief provision to be mutual so that either party can seek an injunction.

findings.quote: Halyard shall reimburse Vedanta upon demand for all costs, charges, and expenses incurred by Vedanta in connection with such proceeding, including without limitation all reasonable attorneys' fees, court fees, expert witness charges, and litigation disbursements, without Vedanta being required to satisfy any reciprocal fee-shifting obligation
findings.why: This is a one-way cost indemnity under which only Halyard pays the other side's legal costs, with no reciprocity.
findings.draft_redline: Delete clause 8.3 and leave costs to the court's discretion under general law.
findings.note_to_counterparty: We cannot agree to one-way costs shifting; we propose leaving costs to the court.

findings.quote: shall cooperate fully with Vedanta at Halyard's expense to mitigate and remediate any harm arising therefrom
findings.why: Imposes an immediate breach notification duty for suspected or threatened incidents and a one-way obligation to remediate at Halyard's own cost, which the playbook does not cover.
findings.draft_redline: "The Receiving Party shall notify the Disclosing Party promptly on becoming aware of any unauthorised disclosure of its Confidential Information and shall reasonably cooperate to limit its effects."
findings.note_to_counterparty: We suggest a mutual notification and reasonable cooperation obligation, without an open-ended obligation to bear remediation costs.

findings.quote: not use, exploit, copy, reproduce, reverse engineer, decompile, disassemble, or derive source code from any Confidential Information
findings.why: Reverse engineering is prohibited, matching the preferred position, although it binds Halyard only.

findings.quote: either Party may assign this Agreement upon written notice to an Affiliate or to a successor entity
findings.why: Assignment needs consent, with a mutual exception to Affiliates or successors on notice.
findings.fallback_cited: Either party may assign to a Group member or successor on notice.

findings.quote: the laws of England and Wales. The Parties irrevocably agree that the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction
findings.why: English law and exclusive English courts match the preferred position.
